title: Credit-Limit Increase Under the Revised Credit Risk Policy
scenario_text:
You are a credit risk manager at Ferrum Capital, a commercial-financing fintech. A wholesale borrower, Talbot Metals, has requested a 70% increase to its revolving credit limit to fund a seasonal inventory build. The relationship manager wants a decision this week.

Active policy: Credit Risk Policy CRP v6, effective 2025-02-01. Credit-limit increases are tiered: up to 25% may be approved by a Credit Analyst; 26-50% requires a Credit Manager plus updated financial statements; anything beyond 50% requires the Credit Committee. CRP v6 lowered the Credit Committee trigger to 'beyond 50%' from the prior 'beyond 100%' under CRP v5, under which a Credit Manager could approve increases up to 100%.

The relationship manager forwards a precedent from the credit log: 2024-09-12, borrower 'Ridgeway Alloys,' 80% limit increase approved directly by Credit Manager Dana Roe with updated financials. Policy version at decision: CRP v5. Note: "Within Credit Manager authority under v5 (<= 100%)."

Current facts: Talbot's updated financials are on file and clean, but no Credit Committee review has been convened. The relationship manager writes: "Dana approved 80% for Ridgeway last fall with just her sign-off. Talbot's ask is smaller at 70%, so this is well within your authority - please approve."
question: State the decision and the single controlling reason as one short phrase.
